Expected number of classes with more than N individuals given parameters \(\theta\) and sample size J using the GEM representation

Source: R/richness.R
kest_gt0.Rd

The expected number of species with more than N individuals is estimated by averaging nrep independent draws of the neutral model with the Griffiths-Engen-McCloskey representation (generate_hoppe_urn()).

Usage

kest_gt0(theta, J, N, nrep = 100)

Arguments

theta

parameter \(\theta\), a positive real value

J

number of individuals, a whole number

N

minimal abundance (a species is counted if its abundance is > N)

nrep

number of simulated communities, at least 2 (default 100)

Value

A list with

k

the expected number of classes with more than N individuals, a real number

sigmak

the standard deviation of that number across the nrep draws, a real number (a measure of the spread of single communities, not the standard error of k)

See also

kest_gt() for a deterministic approximation

Examples

set.seed(1)
kest_gt0(11.3, 234373, 50)
#> $k
#> [1] 63.22
#> 
#> $sigmak
#> [1] 6.178457
#>
